Install Claude Code: **MacOS/Linux (Recommended):** ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):** ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` **Windows (Recommended):** ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ```powershell winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` **NPM (Deprecated):** ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` 2. readmeHtml:
Claude Code

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

Learn more in the official documentation.

Get started

Note

Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.

For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.

  1. Install Claude Code:

    MacOS/Linux (Recommended):

    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

    Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):

    brew install --cask claude-code

    Windows (Recommended):

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

    WinGet (Windows):

    winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

    NPM (Deprecated):

    npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

  2. Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

Plugins

This repository includes several Claude Code plugins that extend functionality with custom commands and agents. See the plugins directory for detailed documentation on available plugins.

Reporting Bugs

We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.

Connect on Discord

Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.

Data collection, usage, and retention

When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.

How we use your data

See our data usage policies.

Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.

For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

releases.name: v2.1.300
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `virtualText` to a mod's prompt decorations: text drawn in the prompt box that never enters the draft or the submitted prompt
- Added `cache_creation_5m_tokens` and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` to the OpenTelemetry `api_request` event, splitting cache writes by lifetime
- Added `$.ui.view({ agentId })` for mods: shows an agent's transcript in the main view when you ask, and `$.ui.view({})` goes back
- Added a `dir` prop on a mod's `Text` for right-to-left text: on Windows and in VS Code's terminal its rows read in that direction and sit flush right
- Added `/advisor` on Claude Platform on AWS; no advisor runs until you pick one with `/advisor`, `advisorModel` or `--advisor`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1` turns it off
- Added OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention attributes to trace spans, such as `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `gen_ai.tool.name` and `error.type`
- Added support for rewriting a workflow agent's `prompt` and `model` in the `agent.spawn` mod hook, which could only refuse workflow agents before
- Added the `prompt.change` mod hook, raised when the prompt box's text changes without a typed edit: a recalled history

releases.name: v2.1.299
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS` environment variable: Claude gets the paths of `@` file mentions to read with its file tools, not the files' contents
- Added idle compaction in the terminal: a 200K+ token conversation left idle for about 54 minutes is compacted before its one-hour prompt cache expires, so your next message doesn't reprocess it all
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` to change idle compaction's 200K-token minimum; `"idleCompaction": false` in settings.json turns it off. Both need v2.1.290 or later
- Added `$.prompt.media` so a `prompt.submit` hook of a mod installed by managed settings can read the bytes of an image or document attached to the prompt
- Added `$.session.identity()` for mods installed by managed settings: how the session is signed in, and its organization and email when managed `forceLoginOrgUUID` lists that organization
- Added `size`, `weight`, `mono` and `tabular` to a mod's `Text` and named spacing steps (`xs` to `xl`) to its `Box`; `bold` is deprecated in favor of `weight`
- Added `--shutdown-drain-sec` to `claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator`: on SIGTERM it stops polling and gives the poll in flight an

releases.name: v2.1.296
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a `code` key to the Claude apps gateway's `managed.policies[]`: the same settings as `cli`, also applied in Claude Desktop's Code tab; beside `desktop`, it turns on Claude Desktop's gateway mode
- Added `autoCompactWindow` to subagent frontmatter and `--agents` definitions, so a subagent can auto-compact earlier than the main conversation's window
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL` to run every workflow agent on one model while other subagents keep theirs
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS` environment variable to set a longer maximum delay for the backoff when retrying an overloaded (529) request
- Added a note in `/plugin` on a plugin whose hooks are left out because another enabled plugin has the same name
- Added an `allow_large` option to the Read tool so Claude can read a text file past the usual size limits in one call when it needs the whole file and the context has room
- Fixed managed-settings `PreToolUse` hooks that deny a tool call with `"continue": false`, and managed `prompt` hooks that block one, refusing the call but not ending the turn
- Fixed PostToolUse hooks in managed settings not applying `updatedMCPToolOut

releases.name: v2.1.295
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `onFailure: "block"` for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can't start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through
- Added Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501) support: terminals that implement it can show whether Claude Code is working, waiting on you, or done
- Added quoted text to the `/copy` picker, so a drafted message copies without its `>` markers
- Added a warning to `claude plugin install`, `enable`, `disable` and `marketplace add` when the settings file they write to does not load
- Added a line on stderr, when it is a terminal, that says what a `claude -p` run is waiting for when it stays open after its last turn
- Added support for `timeouts.upstream_ttfb_ms` on the Claude apps gateway's Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and other cloud upstreams: a value you set now limits how long a stream may take to start there, after which it fails over or gets a 502
- Added a "Backgrounding cancelled" message when you stop the turn while `←` is waiting for the current tool to finish
- Added an optional `models` list to every Claude apps gateway upstream: only the listed models are sent there, on failover too, and o

releases.name: v2.1.294
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Fixed `prompt` and `agent` hooks written as instructions (such as "Block commands that...") allowing what they should block
- Improved how `prompt` hooks on Stop and SubagentStop written as instructions (such as "Carry on if the build is broken") are judged, so Claude is less likely to stop early

aiSummary.oneLiner: An official, terminal-based AI coding assistant powered directly by the Claude model family.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude Code is a command-line interface tool developed by Anthropic that deeply integrates their Claude AI models directly into a developer's local environment. It is designed to understand entire codebases by autonomously navigating directories, reading files, and executing local shell commands for context. The tool assists with complex refactoring, bug hunting, and feature implementation without requiring developers to leave their terminal or copy-paste code into a browser. It maintains a secure, local execution perimeter while leveraging the advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. This drastically reduces context switching and accelerates the software development lifecycle.
keyFeatures: Native terminal integration: Operates entirely within the command line, integrating seamlessly into existing shell environments and workflows.
Autonomous codebase navigation: Capable of searching directories, reading files, and grepping for specific patterns to build context automatically.
Local command execution: Safely runs local tests, linters, and build scripts to verify code changes before finalizing them.
Advanced model reasoning: Powered directly by Anthropic's most capable models, ensuring high-quality architectural advice and code generation.
Context-aware refactoring: Understands the broader repository structure, allowing it to safely execute multi-file changes and updates.

useCases.title: Automated Bug Resolution
useCases.description: Instruct the assistant to locate the source of a specific error trace, write the fix, and run the test suite to verify it.

useCases.title: Complex Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Command the tool to migrate an entire directory of components to a new framework API across multiple interdependent files.

useCases.title: Codebase Onboarding
useCases.description: Ask the terminal assistant to explain the architecture and data flow of a massive, unfamiliar repository dynamically.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Implementation
useCases.description: Describe a new feature in natural language and allow the tool to scaffold the necessary files, logic, and tests automatically.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professional software engineers and developers who prefer working in terminal environments and want powerful, context-aware AI assistance. It requires familiarity with command-line interfaces and local development workflows.
